title: NAT, routing, and gateways (egress without inbound exposure)
hook: Private subnet instances need outbound internet for patches and API calls but should not accept inbound connections from the internet. A Network Address Translation (NAT) Gateway in a public subnet provides one-way egress.

blocks.text: NAT Gateway translates private IP addresses to a public IP for outbound connections. Return traffic is mapped back to the originating instance. NAT Gateway is managed, highly available per Availability Zone, and billed per hour plus data processed. Route tables connect subnets to gateways: 0.0.0.0/0 → NAT for private subnets, 0.0.0.0/0 → Internet Gateway for public subnets. VPC endpoints (Gateway or Interface) route AWS service traffic privately without traversing the public internet or NAT.

entries.plainDefinition: Managed AWS service for outbound internet from private subnets.
entries.example: ECS task in private subnet pulls npm packages via NAT.

entries.plainDefinition: Rules determining where network traffic is directed — local, IGW, NAT, TGW.
entries.example: Private subnet associated with route table pointing to NAT.

entries.plainDefinition: Private connection to AWS services without internet gateway.
entries.example: S3 Gateway endpoint — free, route table entry.

blocks.text: NAT Gateway is a frequent cost surprise in dev accounts left running 24/7. Production designs place one NAT per AZ for resilience — if AZ-a NAT fails, only that AZ's private subnets lose egress. VPC endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB eliminate NAT data processing charges for those services. Interviews ask you to troubleshoot 'private instance cannot reach internet' by checking route table, NAT AZ, and Security Group egress.

blocks.title: Interview framing
blocks.body: NAT for generic internet egress; VPC endpoints for AWS APIs to save cost and improve security.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Instance sends packet
items.body: Destination 203.0.113.50 — route table matches 0.0.0.0/0 → NAT Gateway.

items.title: NAT translates source
items.body: Private IP 10.0.10.5 becomes NAT Gateway public Elastic IP.

items.title: Internet Gateway forwards
items.body: NAT is in public subnet — packet exits via IGW.

items.title: Return path
items.body: Response hits NAT public IP; NAT maps back to 10.0.10.5.

diagram.title: NAT egress path
diagram.source:
flowchart LR
  EC2[Private EC2 10.0.10.5] --> RT[Route table 0.0.0.0/0 to NAT]
  RT --> NAT[NAT Gateway public subnet]
  NAT --> IGW[Internet Gateway]
  IGW --> NET[Internet]

snippet.label: CloudFormation: NAT Gateway with Elastic IP
snippet.code:
Resources:
  NatEIP:
    Type: AWS::EC2::EIP
    DependsOn: InternetGatewayAttachment
    Properties:
      Domain: vpc
  NatGateway:
    Type: AWS::EC2::NatGateway
    Properties:
      AllocationId: !GetAtt NatEIP.AllocationId
      SubnetId: !Ref PublicSubnetA
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: nat-az-a
snippet.explanation: NAT lives in public subnet with Elastic IP. One NAT per AZ for HA — repeat for AZ-b.

snippet.label: CloudFormation: S3 Gateway VPC endpoint
snippet.code:
Resources:
  S3Endpoint:
    Type: AWS::EC2::VPCEndpoint
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref AppVpc
      ServiceName: !Sub com.amazonaws.${AWS::Region}.s3
      RouteTableIds:
        - !Ref PrivateRouteTable
      VpcEndpointType: Gateway
snippet.explanation: Gateway endpoint adds route to S3 prefix list — traffic stays on AWS network, no NAT charge.

snippet.label: CLI: troubleshoot private instance connectivity
snippet.code:
# From private instance — check route and DNS
ip route | grep default
curl -s --max-time 5 https://checkip.amazonaws.com

aws ec2 describe-route-tables \
  --filters Name=association.subnet-id,Values=subnet-private-a \
  --query 'RouteTables[0].Routes'
snippet.explanation: Default route must point to NAT in same AZ. Missing route or wrong AZ NAT is the top cause of egress failure.

blocks.title: NAT vs VPC endpoint vs public subnet
rows: No NAT charge for those resources

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Single NAT in one AZ serving all private subnets — AZ failure kills all egress. Forgetting Elastic IP for NAT. Routing S3 through NAT instead of Gateway endpoint. NAT instance (self-managed) when NAT Gateway is available — more ops burden.

interviewTakeaways: NAT Gateway enables outbound internet from private subnets without inbound exposure.
One NAT per AZ; private subnet route table points 0.0.0.0/0 to NAT in same AZ.
Use S3/DynamoDB Gateway endpoints to avoid NAT data processing charges.
60s: Private egress via NAT in public subnet with EIP. Route table is key. VPC endpoints for AWS services. NAT costs hourly + per GB — common bill surprise.
Follow-up: how does Transit Gateway differ from VPC peering?
commonPitfalls: One NAT for all AZs — AZ outage kills cross-AZ egress for subnets pointing to that NAT.
Strong answer: NAT per AZ, subnet routes to local AZ NAT, endpoints for S3/SQS.
Leaving NAT Gateway running in idle dev VPC over weekends.
Missing default route in private route table — instance has no egress path.

jsTsCorrelations.note: Lambda in private subnet needs NAT or VPC endpoints to reach internet and AWS APIs. Missing endpoint for SQS causes timeouts — not an IAM issue.
